title: Primitive Reflexes and Postural Reactions: The Hidden Timeline of Infant Movement

hook.en: Some reflexes must disappear and others must appear and stay for life. Slide through the first two years and watch which ones are due, fading or overdue.
hook.ur: Kuch reflexes ko ghayab hona chahiye aur kuch ko aana aur umar bhar rehna chahiye. Pehle do saal slide karein aur dekhein kaun se due, khatam hotay ya late hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll describe the main primitive reflexes and postural reactions with their typical windows, test them safely, and explain why a reflex that stays too long, never appears or is asymmetrical matters.
goal.ur: End tak aap aham primitive reflexes aur postural reactions ko un ke typical windows ke saath bayan karenge, mehfooz tareeqe se test karenge, aur samjhayenge ke jo reflex bohat der rahe, kabhi na aaye ya asymmetrical ho woh kyun aham hai.

text.en: A newborn moves with **primitive reflexes**: automatic, stereotyped responses driven by the brainstem and spinal cord. They help survival (rooting, sucking) and prepare movement (grasp, stepping). As the cortex matures it **inhibits** them, usually between 4 and 12 months, and replaces them with **postural reactions**: **righting reactions** keep the head and body aligned, **equilibrium (tilting) reactions** keep the centre of mass over the base, and **protective (parachute) reactions** throw out an arm to save a fall. Primitive reflexes should leave; postural reactions should arrive and stay for life.
text.ur: Nawzaida **primitive reflexes** ke saath harkat karta hai: khud-ba-khud, ek jaise jawabat jo brainstem aur spinal cord se chalte hain. Yeh bachao mein madad karte hain (rooting, sucking) aur harkat ki tayyari karte hain (grasp, stepping). Jaise cortex pukhta hota hai woh unhein **rokta** hai, aam taur par 4 se 12 mahine ke beech, aur unki jagah **postural reactions** aate hain: **righting reactions** sar aur jism ko seedha rakhte hain, **equilibrium (tilting) reactions** markaz-e-saql ko base ke upar rakhte hain, aur **protective (parachute) reactions** girne se bachne ko bazoo phaila dete hain. Primitive reflexes jane chahiye; postural reactions aane aur umar bhar rehne chahiye.

text.en: Think of **scaffolding on a building going up**. Early on the scaffold is essential: it holds the structure while the walls are being built. When the walls can stand, the scaffold must come down or it blocks the windows and doors. Primitive reflexes are the scaffold; postural reactions are the walls, which stay. A building with the scaffold still up long after the walls are finished, or with no walls, both need attention.
text.ur: **Ban rahi imarat par scaffolding** tasawwur karein. Shuru mein scaffold zaroori hai: jab deewarein ban rahi hon tab yeh dhancha thaamta hai. Jab deewarein khud khari ho sakein to scaffold utarna chahiye warna khirkiyan aur darwazay band kar deta hai. Primitive reflexes scaffold hain; postural reactions deewarein, jo rehti hain. Woh imarat jis ka scaffold deewarein bannay ke bohat baad tak laga rahe, ya jis ki deewarein hi na hon, dono tawajjo maangti hain.

intro.en: Slide the corrected age. Under "Primitive reflexes" each bar is the typical window and the status chip says whether that reflex is due, fading or should already be gone. Switch to "Postural reactions" and see the opposite: they are not expected yet, then due, then should stay. Tap a reflex to read how to elicit it and why it matters.
intro.ur: Corrected age slide karein. "Primitive reflexes" mein har bar typical window hai aur status chip batata hai ke woh reflex maujood hona chahiye, khatam ho raha hai ya ab tak ghayab hona chahiye. "Postural reactions" par jayein to ulta dikhta hai: pehle expected nahi, phir due, phir rehni chahiye. Kisi reflex par tap kar ke parhein ke use kaise nikalte hain aur kyun aham hai.

question.en: A 9-month-old still shows a strong, symmetrical Moro reflex whenever his head drops. What is the best interpretation?
question.ur: 9 mahine ke bachay mein jab bhi sar girta hai to mazboot, symmetrical Moro reflex ab bhi maujood hai. Behtareen tabsira kya hai?

text.en: It has persisted beyond its usual window (about 4 to 6 months): look at tone, other reflexes and development, and refer for review
text.ur: Yeh apne aam window (taqreeban 4 se 6 mahine) se zyada rah gaya hai: tone, doosre reflexes aur development dekhein aur review ke liye refer karein

feedback.en: Yes — a strong Moro after about 6 months suggests delayed inhibition and should be reviewed alongside the rest of the examination, not judged alone.
feedback.ur: Haan — taqreeban 6 mahine ke baad mazboot Moro inhibition mein deri dikhata hai aur poore examination ke saath review hona chahiye, akela nahi.

text.en: It is normal; Moro lasts for life
text.ur: Yeh normal hai; Moro umar bhar rehta hai

feedback.en: The Moro (startle) reflex is primitive and should fade by about 4 to 6 months. The startle response in adults is a different reaction.
feedback.ur: Moro (startle) reflex primitive hai aur taqreeban 4 se 6 mahine tak khatam ho jana chahiye. Baalighon ki startle response alag reaction hai.

text.en: It is a good sign of strength
text.ur: Yeh taqat ki achhi nishani hai

feedback.en: Strong persistence is a sign of delayed brain maturation, not strength.
feedback.ur: Mazboot taur par rehna dimagh ki sust pukhtagi ki nishani hai, taqat ki nahi.

hint.en: Primitive reflexes should be integrated (gone) by their window.
hint.ur: Primitive reflexes apne window tak integrate (khatam) hone chahiye.

text.en: **Postural reactions** are tested by tilting and tipping. **Head righting** (from about 3 months) keeps the head upright when the body tilts. **Parachute reactions** appear in sequence: **forward** at about 6 months, **sideways** at about 7, **backward** at about 9, and make independent sitting safe. **Equilibrium reactions** arrive in each posture as it is learned: prone and supine at about 6 months, sitting at 7 to 8, hands and knees at about 9 to 12 months, and standing from about a year. Walking becomes safe only when the equilibrium reactions in standing are present.
text.ur: **Postural reactions** tilt aur tip karke test hote hain. **Head righting** (taqreeban 3 mahine se) jism tirchha hone par sar ko seedha rakhta hai. **Parachute reactions** tarteeb se aate hain: **forward** taqreeban 6 mahine, **sideways** taqreeban 7, **backward** taqreeban 9, aur akelay baithna mehfooz banate hain. **Equilibrium reactions** har posture mein usay seekhte hi aate hain: prone aur supine taqreeban 6 mahine, sitting 7 se 8, haathon aur ghutnon par taqreeban 9 se 12 mahine, aur khare hone mein taqreeban ek saal se. Chalna tabhi mehfooz hota hai jab khare hone ki equilibrium reactions maujood hon.

question.en: An 11-month-old can sit only when propped, and does not throw out his arms sideways or backwards when tipped. Which interpretation fits best?
question.ur: 11 mahine ka bachcha sirf sahare se baith sakta hai aur tip karne par bazoo side ya peechay nahi phailata. Kaunsa tabsira sab se behtar hai?

text.en: Parachute reactions are delayed, so sitting is unsafe and the child needs review of tone and posture
text.ur: Parachute reactions late hain, is liye baithna mehfooz nahi aur bachay ke tone aur posture ka review chahiye

feedback.en: Yes — sideways and backward parachutes should be present by about 9 months. Their absence puts the child at risk of falling over without protecting himself.
feedback.ur: Haan — sideways aur backward parachutes taqreeban 9 mahine tak maujood hone chahiye. Un ki ghair-maujoodgi bachay ko bina bachaaye gir jane ke khatre mein daalti hai.

text.en: Normal: parachute reactions are not expected before 12 months
text.ur: Normal: parachute reactions 12 mahine se pehle expected nahi

feedback.en: They appear between 6 and 9 months. At 11 months they should be there.
feedback.ur: Yeh 6 se 9 mahine ke beech aate hain. 11 mahine par honay chahiye.

text.en: The Moro reflex has simply not faded yet
text.ur: Moro reflex abhi tak khatam nahi hua

feedback.en: The Moro and the parachute are different things: one should disappear, the other should arrive.
feedback.ur: Moro aur parachute alag cheezein hain: ek ko jana chahiye, doosray ko aana chahiye.

text.en: **"Fade by six, parachute by nine."** The Moro, ATNR, TLR, palmar grasp and Galant fade by about 4 to 6 months; the three parachutes (forward, sideways, backward) are all in place by about 9 months, and equilibrium reactions in standing by a year or so. The Babinski sign is the slow one: it can last up to about 2 years.
text.ur: **"Chhe tak khatam, nau tak parachute."** Moro, ATNR, TLR, palmar grasp aur Galant taqreeban 4 se 6 mahine tak khatam; teenon parachutes (forward, sideways, backward) taqreeban 9 mahine tak maujood, aur khare hone ki equilibrium reactions taqreeban ek saal tak. Babinski sign sab se aahista hai: taqreeban 2 saal tak reh sakta hai.

rows.ur: Brainstem aur spinal reflexes: bachao aur shuruati harkat ki mashq

rows.en: Present at birth, fade by 4 to 12 months: Moro, ATNR, palmar grasp, rooting
rows.ur: Paidaish par maujood, 4 se 12 mahine tak khatam: Moro, ATNR, palmar grasp, rooting

rows.ur: Cortical aur brainstem reactions jo posture rakhti aur girne se bachati hain

rows.en: Appear from 3 months and stay for life: righting, equilibrium, parachute
rows.ur: 3 mahine se aati hain aur umar bhar rehti hain: righting, equilibrium, parachute

rows.ur: Cortical, maqsad-wali harkat, upar ke dono par bani hui

rows.en: Reaching, rolling, crawling, walking: only smooth when the primitive reflexes have faded
rows.ur: Pakadna, palatna, rengna, chalna: tabhi hamwar jab primitive reflexes khatam ho chuke ho

text.en: **Testing at the wrong moment, or reading one reflex alone.** Reflexes are unreliable if the baby is crying, hungry, asleep or just fed, so test when calm and awake. A single reflex slightly past its window is a note, not a diagnosis, and windows differ by a month or two between sources. The most important finding is not "present" or "absent" but **asymmetry**, **absence at birth**, or a reflex that is **obligatory** (the baby cannot move out of it). And use the **corrected** age for a premature baby, otherwise you will think a normal baby's reflexes are overdue.
text.ur: **Ghalat waqt par test ya sirf ek reflex parhna.** Bachcha ro raha ho, bhooka ho, so raha ho ya abhi doodh piya ho to reflexes bharosay ke nahi hotay, is liye shaant aur jaagte waqt test karein. Apne window se thora sa baahar ek reflex note hai, tashkhees nahi, aur windows mukhtalif kitabon mein ek do mahine ka farq rakhte hain. Sab se aham finding "maujood" ya "ghayab" nahi, balke **asymmetry**, **paidaish par ghair-maujoodgi**, ya aisa reflex hai jo **lazmi (obligatory)** ho (bachcha us se nikal nahi sakta). Aur qabl-az-waqt bachay ke liye **corrected** umar istemal karein, warna normal bachay ke reflexes aap ko late lagen ge.

title.ur: Moro reflex ko mehfooz tareeqe se nikalna

steps.title: Pick the moment
steps.detail: A calm, awake, recently fed baby on a firm, warm surface; keep the room quiet. || Waqt chunein

steps.title: Support the head and trunk
steps.detail: With the baby on his back, lift the shoulders slightly with both hands under the trunk and support the head with one hand. || Sar aur dhar ko sahara dein

steps.title: Let the head drop gently
steps.detail: Allow the head to drop back a few centimetres into your supporting hand: a brisk, small movement only. || Sar ko aahista girne dein

steps.title: Watch both sides together
steps.detail: The arms should abduct and extend, the hands open, then the arms come back toward the chest, and the baby may cry. Compare left and right. || Dono taraf ek saath dekhein

steps.title: Record and calm
steps.detail: Note the intensity, symmetry and age. Pick the baby up and settle him; do not repeat many times. || Likhein aur shaant karein

text.en: **Write the reflex findings as a short table.** "Corrected age 5 months. Moro: symmetrical, weak. ATNR: asymmetrical response, right side stronger, can break out of it. Palmar grasp: absent. Head righting: present. Parachute forward: not yet expected." Report the asymmetry and any obligatory response to the doctor or paediatric team, and give the parents one simple message: "These reflexes are part of normal development; we are checking they leave on time."
text.ur: **Reflex findings ek chhoti table ki tarah likhein.** "Corrected age 5 mahine. Moro: symmetrical, kamzor. ATNR: asymmetrical jawab, right taraf mazboot, us se nikal sakta hai. Palmar grasp: ghayab. Head righting: maujood. Parachute forward: abhi expected nahi." Asymmetry aur kisi lazmi jawab ki doctor ya paediatric team ko report karein, aur walidain ko ek saada paigham dein: "Yeh reflexes normal development ka hissa hain; hum dekh rahe hain ke woh waqt par khatam ho rahe hain."

text.en: Primitive reflexes are part of structured infant neurological examinations such as the **Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE)**, which scores tone, posture, reflexes and movement and helps predict cerebral palsy from about 3 months. However, an isolated primitive reflex has limited predictive value; the strongest early predictor of cerebral palsy is the **General Movements Assessment (fidgety movements at 3 to 5 months)**, combined with HINE and neuroimaging. Descriptions of how the grasp and Moro reflexes fade also show that the sequence is orderly: lower reflexes drop away as higher cortical control takes over.
text.ur: Primitive reflexes structured infant neurological examinations jaise **Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE)** ka hissa hain, jo tone, posture, reflexes aur harkat ko score karta hai aur taqreeban 3 mahine se cerebral palsy ka andaza lagane mein madad deta hai. Magar akela primitive reflex ki predictive value mehdood hai; cerebral palsy ka sab se mazboot shuruati predictor **General Movements Assessment (3 se 5 mahine par fidgety movements)** hai, jo HINE aur neuroimaging ke saath milaya jata hai. Grasp aur Moro reflexes ke khatam hone ki tafseelat bhi dikhati hain ke silsila munazzam hai: neechay ke reflexes jaise jaise cortical control sambhalta hai gir jate hain.

text.en: **Refer promptly for:** a Moro that is absent or clearly asymmetrical (think clavicle fracture, brachial plexus injury or hemiparesis), primitive reflexes still strong after 6 months, any obligatory reflex, absent protective reactions by 10 months, marked floppiness or stiffness, a persistent fisted hand beyond 4 months, or any loss of skills. Handle newborns gently with full head support, avoid repeated startle testing and do not test a baby with a suspected fracture or acute illness.
text.ur: **Foran refer karein:** Moro ghayab ya saaf asymmetrical (clavicle fracture, brachial plexus injury ya hemiparesis sochein), 6 mahine ke baad bhi mazboot primitive reflexes, koi bhi lazmi reflex, 10 mahine tak protective reactions ghayab, wazeh dheelapan ya sakhti, 4 mahine ke baad bhi musalsal band mutthi, ya koi hunar kho dena. Nawzaida ko mukammal sar ke sahare ke saath narmi se handle karein, baar baar startle test na karein aur shak wale fracture ya shadeed bimari mein bachay ka test na karein.

why.ur: Palmar grasp taqreeban 5 se 6 mahine tak khatam hota hai taake haath khul aur chhor sake.

why.ur: Protective reaction hai: taqreeban 7 mahine tak aani chahiye aur umar bhar rehti hai.

text.ur: Sitting mein equilibrium reactions

text.en: Asymmetrical tonic neck reflex (ATNR)
text.ur: Asymmetrical tonic neck reflex (ATNR)

why.en: The ATNR fades by about 6 months; if obligatory, the baby cannot roll or bring hands together.
why.ur: ATNR taqreeban 6 mahine tak khatam ho jata hai; lazmi ho to bachcha palat ya haath jorr nahi sakta.

question.en: Why does an ATNR that persists stop a baby from rolling and reaching to the midline?
question.ur: Ruka hua ATNR bachay ko palatne aur midline tak pohanchne se kyun rokta hai?

answer.en: The ATNR makes the arm and leg on the side he faces **extend**, and the other side **flex**, whenever the head turns. A baby who must turn his head to look at a toy gets one arm shot out and the other bent, so he cannot bring both hands together, cannot watch his own hand reach, and cannot flex both sides together to roll. The reflex "wins" over the voluntary plan, which is why an obligatory ATNR is a red flag.
answer.ur: ATNR jab bhi sar ghoomta hai to jis taraf chehra ho us side ka bazoo aur taang **extend** aur doosri side **flex** karta hai. Jo bachcha khilone ko dekhne ke liye sar ghumata hai uska ek bazoo phail jata aur doosra mur jata hai, is liye woh dono haath jorr nahi sakta, apne haath ko pakadte dekh nahi sakta, aur palatne ke liye dono taraf flex nahi kar sakta. Reflex iradi plan par "ghalib" aa jata hai, isi liye lazmi ATNR red flag hai.

question.ur: 2 mahine ke bachay mein sab se pareshan-kun finding kaunsi hai?

text.en: A present, symmetrical rooting reflex
text.ur: Maujood, symmetrical rooting reflex

feedback.en: Rooting is expected at this age.
feedback.ur: Is umar mein rooting expected hai.

text.en: A strong palmar grasp
text.ur: Mazboot palmar grasp

feedback.en: A palmar grasp is expected at 2 months.
feedback.ur: 2 mahine mein palmar grasp expected hai.

text.ur: Asymmetrical ya ghayab Moro reflex aur ek taraf latka hua dhila bazoo

feedback.en: Yes — it can point to a fracture of the collarbone, a brachial plexus injury or hemiparesis, and needs prompt review.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh collarbone ke fracture, brachial plexus injury ya hemiparesis ki taraf ishara kar sakta hai aur jaldi review chahiye.

summary.en: Primitive reflexes (Moro, ATNR, grasp, rooting) are present at birth and fade by 4 to 12 months; postural reactions (righting, equilibrium, parachute) appear from 3 months and stay for life.
summary.ur: Primitive reflexes (Moro, ATNR, grasp, rooting) paidaish par maujood aur 4 se 12 mahine tak khatam; postural reactions (righting, equilibrium, parachute) 3 mahine se aate aur umar bhar rehte hain.

summary.en: Test a calm, awake baby by corrected age, and look for asymmetry, absence at birth and obligatory reflexes more than for one reflex slightly late.
summary.ur: Shaant, jagte bachay ko corrected umar ke hisab se test karein, aur ek reflex ke thora late hone se zyada asymmetry, paidaish par ghair-maujoodgi aur lazmi reflexes dekhein.

summary.en: Persisting primitive reflexes block rolling, reaching and standing; missing parachute reactions make sitting and walking unsafe: refer promptly.
summary.ur: Rukay hue primitive reflexes palatne, pakadne aur khare hone ko rokte hain; ghayab parachute reactions baithna aur chalna ghair-mehfooz bana deti hain: jaldi refer karein.

front.en: Name three primitive reflexes and when they fade.
front.ur: Teen primitive reflexes batayein aur woh kab khatam hotay hain.

back.en: Moro about 4 to 6 months; palmar grasp about 5 to 6 months; ATNR about 6 months (Babinski up to about 2 years).
back.ur: Moro taqreeban 4 se 6 mahine; palmar grasp taqreeban 5 se 6 mahine; ATNR taqreeban 6 mahine (Babinski taqreeban 2 saal tak).

front.en: When do the parachute reactions appear?

back.en: Forward about 6 months, sideways about 7, backward about 9; they stay for life.
back.ur: Forward taqreeban 6 mahine, sideways taqreeban 7, backward taqreeban 9; umar bhar rehti hain.

back.en: A reflex so strong the child cannot move out of it, for example an ATNR that always pulls the arm out when the head turns; a red flag.
back.ur: Itna mazboot reflex ke bachcha us se nikal nahi sakta, maslan ATNR jo sar ghumne par hamesha bazoo phaila deta hai; red flag.

front.en: Why use the corrected age for reflexes?
front.ur: Reflexes ke liye corrected umar kyun?

back.en: A baby born early has had less time to mature, so judge reflexes by calendar age minus the weeks born early, until 24 months.
back.ur: Qabl-az-waqt paida bachay ko pukhta hone ka kam waqt mila, is liye reflexes ko 24 mahine tak calendar umar minus pehle paida hone ke hafte se parkhein.
